clue.text: Stripping cover, bang on about nurse

indicators.note: taking the covering off a word strips away its outside letters, leaving only the inner ones

parts.note: bang without its first and last letters

indicators.note: turning something about faces it the other way, so the word for on is read backwards

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: Someone harps on about a nurse, presumably after stripping off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang on about' reads as nagging, but 'on' is the cricket term and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind, devoted nurse is proverbially called an angel, as in 'ministering angel'.

clue.text: Sparks essentially fixes bright lights

indicators.note: the essence of a word is at its heart, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the six
clamps means fixes or fastens firmly

explanation.surface: The setter, Sparks, is at heart someone who mends bright lights, like an electrician.
explanation.walkthrough: Sparks is the setter's pseudonym and also slang for an electrician, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Arc lamps give intense light from an electric arc between two electrodes, used in floodlights and searchlights.

clue.text: Fitted in Jag, a rotten choke

indicators.note: something fitted in is tucked inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: found across the three words

explanation.surface: A dodgy part has been fitted in a Jaguar car, and its choke is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jag is a Jaguar car, and a choke is a carburettor valve, which suits a mechanic's complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To garrotte someone is to strangle them, so it is a verb meaning choke.

clue.text: Becket, say, cut off old bores

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into something, so the old letter goes inside the cutting word

parts.note: to lop is to cut off a branch or limb
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Thomas Becket, say, cut short tedious old people.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Becket the martyred archbishop is the obvious reading, but a becket is a sailor's term for a rope eye or loop; 'bores' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A becket is a length of rope with a knot at one end and an eye at the other, an example of a nautical loop.

clue.text: Introduced new series in self-deprecation

indicators.note: making something new from old material means its letters are put into a fresh order
a series is an unbroken run, so a consecutive stretch of letters from inside the longer phrase is taken

parts.note: the letters running from the end of self through the start of deprecation

explanation.surface: Someone opened a new set of talks or books with a modest, self-mocking remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen hides the join: the letters straddle 'self' and 'deprecation' before being rearranged. 'New series' looks like a TV phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To preface something is to introduce it with opening remarks, so prefaced is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Issue warning edict or a threat will develop

indicators.note: when something develops it changes form, so these letters are rearranged into a new phrase

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a decree or menace is going to escalate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a British law read out to unruly crowds ordering them to disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: To read the riot act is an idiom for giving someone a stern warning or reprimand.

clue.text: Maybe Paisley's sound — fine then depressed

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
feeling low means depressed

explanation.surface: Ian Paisley's voice: first all right, then gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: Paisley suggests the Northern Irish preacher's booming voice, but it is a Scottish town and 'sound' means a sea inlet; flow is a Scots word for one, as in Scapa Flow.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a flow is a sea basin or sound, as in Scapa Flow in Orkney, so a Paisley speaker might use it.

clue.text: Herb in cold and hot chopped liver

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: chopped food is cut up and tossed together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe: a herb in a dish of cold and hot chopped liver.
explanation.definitionFit: Chervil is a delicate culinary herb of the parsley family, used in French cooking.

clue.text: Turf rolled over bare plots treated with something

indicators.note: turf rolled over is flipped upside down, which in a down entry puts its letters in reverse

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf

indicators.note: stripped bare means the outside is taken away, leaving only the inner letters

parts.note: plots are beds in a garden; beds stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: Turf has been laid over bare garden plots treated with fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: Plots here are garden beds, and only their middle survives once stripped bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosed means given a dose of something such as medicine, so it means treated with a substance.

clue.text: Those aiming to cut masses in, say, Kensington church inspired by blues legend

parts.note: W8 is the London postal district for Kensington; said out loud, the 8 is spelt as a word

indicators.note: something inspired is breathed in, so the church goes inside the blues name

parts.note: Muddy Waters, the Chicago blues guitarist and singer
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Slimmers in a Kensington church inspired by a famous blues musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masses' looks like church services, but it means body mass. W8, spoken, becomes W EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight Watchers members are dieters trying to reduce their body mass, so they aim to cut masses.

clue.text: Gradually weaken staff in centre

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it, so the staff word sits inside the centre word

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Morale in head office is being slowly undermined among the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but here it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrosion eats metal away slowly, so figuratively to corrode is to wear down or undermine bit by bit.

clue.text: Birds flying to caves

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a different order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A flock of birds heads off to roost in caves.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocets are elegant wading birds with upturned bills, the emblem of the RSPB.

clue.text: Punt worker, say, back in Cambridge

parts.note: a worker is an example of an ant, the caste that does the labour

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its closing letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of the city

explanation.surface: A boatman poling a punt back on the Cam in Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Punting is a famous Cambridge pastime, but here 'Punt' is a bet. 'Say' marks the worker as one example of an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A punt is a wager, and an ante is the stake put in before a poker hand.

clue.text: Stone Age spans origins of ancient tools

indicators.note: something that spans another stretches right across it, holding it within

parts.note: taken as written; it goes around the inserted pair

indicators.note: the origin of each word is where it starts, so just the opening letters are taken

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: The Stone Age covers the beginnings of primitive tool-making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone Age' looks like one phrase; split it, and 'Stone' is the definition while 'Age' is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone, a variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: Greedy biblical king banishing first daughter

indicators.note: banishing sends something away, and first places that removal at the front

parts.note: David, king of Israel in the Old Testament
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A covetous Old Testament monarch exiles his eldest girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First daughter' reads as an eldest child; it is the letter D removed from the front of the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or keen, and in the sense of craving more it can mean greedy, as in avid for gain.

clue.text: Attempt to plug record upset novelist and playwright

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down entry turns the letters upside down
a plug fills a hole, so the attempt word is pushed inside the record word

parts.note: a log is a written record
a go is an attempt or try

explanation.surface: A bid to promote an album upsets a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The attempt sits between the second and third letters of the record before the whole is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was the Russian author of the novel Dead Souls and the play The Government Inspector.

clue.text: Name sources in criminal enterprise long before hint of enquiry breaks

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the single letter goes into the group
the source of a word is where it begins, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: first letters of the four words

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone names the origins of a criminal racket long before the first sign of an investigation breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a big name.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeb, short for celebrity, is a famous person, a 'name' in the sense of 'a big name'.

clue.text: Noble quietly retracted warning caught by heavenly maiden

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: a thing caught by another is held within it, so the warning goes inside the heavenly word

parts.note: ethereal means heavenly or celestial

indicators.note: something retracted is drawn back, so the warning word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the golfer's shouted warning
M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A nobleman softly withdraws a warning after being captivated by an angelic young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed golf cry sits after the first letter of the heavenly word. 'Maiden' is a cricket over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the realm is a member of the British nobility entitled to sit in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Omitting introduction, author into debauchery pens better adventure

indicators.note: to pen something is to shut it in an enclosure, so the better word goes inside
leaving out the introduction means dropping the opening letter

parts.note: the Marquis de Sade, the writer whose name gave us sadism
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A writer drawn into dissolute living produces an even better story of daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' suggests writing, which suits an author, but here it means encloses; 'better' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or reckless exploit, so it is a synonym for an adventure.

clue.text: Mostly Vatican restored damaged ceramics and textiles?

definitions.text: Mostly Vatican restored damaged ceramics and textiles?

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: the Vatican less its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pottery and fabrics from the Vatican were mostly mended after being harmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restored' looks like the indicator, but it is fodder; 'damaged' does the rearranging. The whole clue doubles as a description of what the Vatican's collections contain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramics and textiles are examples of the decorative arts, crafts valued for ornament as well as use, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Green half of neighbourhood with uncrowned talent

indicators.note: a crown sits on top, so removing it takes away the first letter
half a word is one of its two equal parts, here the opening four letters

parts.note: the first half of environs, a word for neighbourhood
nous is practical intelligence or know-how

explanation.surface: Feeling jealous of half the area's gifts, which lack a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a colour or a village green beside 'neighbourhood', but here it means jealous.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is the colour of envy, as in green with envy, so green means envious.

clue.text: Turner picked up in its original condition?

indicators.text: picked up in its original condition
indicators.note: picked up means read upwards in a down entry, and the word stays unchanged when read that way

parts.note: something that turns

explanation.surface: A Turner painting is collected in pristine condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner suggests the painter J M W Turner and his canvases; here it is anything that turns, and the word reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is a device or muscle that rotates, so literally a turner.

clue.text: Papers backing very American, look-at-me sort?

indicators.note: backing up means moving in reverse, so the papers abbreviation runs from right to left

parts.note: ID is identity papers
V is the abbreviation for very
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Newspapers championing a very American attention-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers backing' suggests press support, but papers are identity documents turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a temperamental, self-important star who demands attention, hence a show-off.

clue.text: Discourage one of 9, perhaps, but not 1

indicators.note: but not excludes something, so the numeral is taken out of the word

parts.note: 9 down are slimmers, and each one is someone on a diet
the numeral one as the Roman letter

explanation.surface: Put someone off a slimming club, though not the first one.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 and 1 look like references to other clues; 9 is, but 1 is simply the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to put them off or dissuade them, so it is a synonym for discourage.

clue.text: Shrewd copper irritated fences

indicators.note: to fence something is to enclose it, so the irritated word surrounds the copper

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means irritated or bothered
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A sharp policeman, annoyed, is dealing in stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'fences' suggest police and receivers of stolen goods; in fact copper is the metal and fences means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute means sharp, and a sharp or acute mind is a shrewd, perceptive one.

clue.text: Intermittently picked out Neptunian volcano

indicators.note: picking at intervals, on and off, means taking every other letter of the word

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Astronomers occasionally spot a volcano on the planet Neptune.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is Europe's highest active volcano, on the east coast of Sicily.

clue.text: Canine left wearing half-hearted canine expression?

indicators.note: something worn is put on and around, so the expression surrounds the left letter
a half-hearted word loses half of its heart, so one of its two central letters goes

parts.note: the sound a dog makes
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A dog barks feebly, with a second dog's expression worn on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: The canine in the definition is a different animal from the one doing the barking.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolf is the wild canine from which the domestic dog descends.

clue.text: Water sport with its final coming up … here?

definitions.text: Water sport with its final coming up … here?

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means moving higher, so the final letter swaps places with the one above it

parts.note: water polo, or simply polo, the team ball game

explanation.surface: Asks where water polo, with its final match imminent, might be played.
explanation.walkthrough: The ending of the sport climbs one place; the whole clue then suggests where water polo is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Water polo is played in a swimming pool, so the pool is the place meant by here.

clue.text: Couple starts to talk with others a little

indicators.note: the start of each word is its opening letter, so only those are taken

parts.note: the initial letters of the three words
some means a little, as in 'have some'

explanation.surface: A pair begin to chat a bit with other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair of people together, so it is a synonym for a couple.

clue.text: Foreign agents arresting informer drilled by old republic

indicators.note: arresting someone means taking them in and holding them, so the agents enclose the informer

parts.note: the US Central Intelligence Agency works abroad

indicators.note: something drilled has a hole bored through it, with the old letter put inside

parts.note: a rat is someone who informs on others
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Overseas spies seize a grass who was trained by a former state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old republic' looks like the definition, but 'old' is O, bored into the informer; the answer is a modern republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a republic in south-east Europe, independent of Yugoslavia since 1991.

clue.text: Was excited to an extent about France's seafood

indicators.note: going about something means going round it, so the two pieces surround the country letter

parts.note: rose, as in passions rose, meaning grew excited
the suffix -ish means to some extent
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Someone got a little worked up about French seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: The two outer pieces join and hold the French letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The rosefish, also called ocean perch or redfish, is an edible North Atlantic fish, hence seafood.

clue.text: Big pair of hands carrying a case of Grenache

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so the pair of hands enclose the single letter

parts.note: left and right, abbreviated L and R
taken as written

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the grape

explanation.surface: Two big hands carrying a crate of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A case of Grenache' sounds like a dozen bottles; the case is just the outer letters, with 'a' held by the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and big are straightforward synonyms describing great size.
